chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the bequest for the inheritor, so he said: 'It is permissible.'
He said: Then he recited this verse:
'If he leaves behind wealth, the bequest is for the parents and near relatives.'

key_terms.الوارث: Inheritor/heir — one entitled to receive a share of the estate according to the Quran's laws of inheritance
key_terms.الوصية: Bequest/will (wasiyya) — a testamentary disposition of one's estate made before death, distinct from the laws of inheritance (mirath)
key_terms.تجوز: It is permissible (tajuzu) — the legal ruling indicating the act is lawful, derived from the root jawaz (permissibility)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law to make a bequest for an heir who already inherits?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Muhammad ibn Muslim asks Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) whether a dying person may make a bequest (wasiyya) in favor of an heir who is already entitled to inherit. The Imam affirms this is permissible, then cites Quran 2:180 as the scriptural basis — a verse that explicitly commands making a bequest for parents and near relatives. This ruling addresses a jurisprudential question debated among early Muslim jurists: some held that a bequest for an heir was automatically void since they receive their share through the laws of inheritance, but the Imam here establishes that such a bequest is valid.
